facts.label: reported
facts.quote: These discussions failed, and Lehman filed a Chapter 11 petition that remains the largest bankruptcy filing in U.S. history, involving more than US$600 billion in assets.
facts.text: Lehman Brothers filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on September 15, 2008, holding more than 600 billion USD in assets, making it the largest bankruptcy filing in United States history.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: During the 2008 global financial crisis, the BSE SENSEX experienced a sharp decline. It dropped from over 21,000 points in January 2008 to below 8,000 points in October 2008.
facts.text: During the 2008 global financial crisis, the BSE Sensex plummeted from above 21,000 points in January 2008 to below 8,000 points by October 2008.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: The BSE Sensex fell to a low of 8160 on March 9, 2009, witnessing a decline of 60.9 per cent from the peak of 20,873 on January 8, 2008.
facts.text: The BSE Sensex touched an intra-crisis trough of 8,160 on March 9, 2009, recording a cumulative drop of 60.9 percent from its January 2008 high.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: The capital flight that ensued in the wake of the crisis deprived Indian equity markets of FII investments to the tune of around Rs.48,249 crore (US$ 10,439 million) during 2008-09.
facts.text: Global capital flight caused foreign institutional investors to withdraw 48,249 crore INR from Indian equities during fiscal year 2008-09.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: In response to the knock-on effects of the global economic crisis on the Indian economy, since October 11, 2008 the Reserve Bank has reduced the CRR by a cumulative 400 basis points to 5.0 per cent of NDTL, the repo rate by 425 basis points to 4.75 per cent and the reverse repo rate by 275 basis points to 3.25 per cent.
facts.text: The Reserve Bank of India reduced the benchmark repo rate by 425 basis points down to 4.75 percent to ease borrowing costs and home loan EMIs.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: After clocking an average of 9.4 per cent during three successive years from 2005-06 to 2007-08, the growth rate of real GDP slowed down to 6.7 per cent (revised estimates) in 2008-09.
facts.text: India's real GDP growth rate slowed down to 6.7 percent in 2008-09 from an average of 9.4 percent in the previous three years.

facts.label: reported
facts.text: After tumbling 51.79 percent in 2008, the benchmark NIFTY 50 surged by 75.76 percent in 2009, strongly lifting SIP portfolios that stayed invested through the downturn.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Hence, in the interest of maintaining financial stability, the RBI instituted a 14-day special repo facility for a notified amount of about $ 4 billion to alleviate liquidity stress faced by mutual funds, and banks were allowed temporary use of Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) securities for collateral purposes for an additional 0.5 per cent of Net Demand and Time Liabilities exclusively for this.
facts.text: To prevent panic redemptions from hurting mutual funds and retail unitholders, the Reserve Bank instituted a special 14-day repo facility providing 4 billion USD in liquidity support.
